deck.title: Traffic Wizard — analytics, minus the sorcery degree

props.title: Traffic ==Wizard==.
props.subtitle: Website analytics, minus the sorcery degree required to read them.

slides.notes: Set the tone: this is a friendly tool, not another dashboard. One sentence — it turns traffic numbers into plain-language answers.

left.label: Your dashboard
left.title: Charts, acronyms, jargon
points: Six tabs to answer one question
Still unsure what to do Monday

slides.notes: Owners of small sites don't want analytics — they want answers. Every chart on the left is standing between them and the three questions on the right.

messages.text: How did my site do this week?
Traffic is up 32%, mostly from a Reddit post that linked your guide on Tuesday.
What should I do about it?
Two moves this week: reply to that thread, and add a follow-up post — visitors from Reddit bounce before page two.

slides.notes: This is the product in one exchange: what changed, what likely caused it, and the one or two moves worth making this week.

items.title: Connect your stats
items.body: Point the Wizard at the traffic data your site already collects.

items.title: It scans for signals
items.body: Spikes, drops, top sources, and the pages quietly on the move.

items.title: You get a briefing
items.body: A short, readable summary — changes, likely causes, suggested moves.

slides.notes: Three beats. The magic is step two: the Wizard does the pattern-hunting a human analyst would do, then writes it up.

props.label: Why a wizard?
props.text: A little theatre makes the numbers approachable. The ==persona== keeps it friendly — the read underneath stays ==honest== and data-first.

slides.notes: The costume is the point: wizardry is a promise that the tool does the hard reading for you. Under the hood it's plain, honest analysis.

tiles.title: Change alerts
tiles.body: Spikes and drops flagged the moment they happen — with the likely cause.

tiles.title: Plain-language briefings
tiles.body: No jargon. What changed, why, and what to try next.

tiles.title: Source spotlight
tiles.body: See which channels are actually sending people.

tiles.title: Pages on the move
tiles.body: The URLs quietly rising — or quietly slipping.

tiles.title: This week's moves
tiles.body: One or two concrete actions, not forty metrics.

slides.notes: Don't read every tile. Highlight change alerts and this week's moves — the two features that replace a dashboard habit.
